clue.text: Protective covering quickly attached to vehicle

indicators.note: one word is joined onto the end of another, so the two pieces simply sit side by side

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
apace is an old word for quickly

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly bolts a protective cover onto a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the speed word first, but 'attached to vehicle' puts it after the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crab, a shield for the animal's body.

clue.text: Concern initially about vessel containing small crack

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so one piece sits inside the other
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of concern
re means about or concerning
a vase is a vessel for flowers
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Worry arises over a pot with a hairline crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep open fissure in a glacier or ice sheet, a very large crack.

clue.text: Supply assistant, admitting offence, completely upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, and completely means the whole combination is turned
admitting means letting in, so one word is placed inside another

parts.note: an assistant is a helper
a sin is an offence

explanation.surface: An aide who has confessed to wrongdoing is thoroughly distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to restock or refill, providing a fresh supply of something used up.

clue.text: Put under pressure in drama

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so this piece comes second

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A character is put under strain in a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a dramatic work written for performance by actors in a theatre.

clue.text: Strange change in latter system keeping place warm

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the letters take on an odd new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd alteration to the second of two systems keeps a home cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Central heating warms a whole building from one boiler through pipes and radiators.

clue.text: Problem created by show-off

definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who strikes affected attitudes

explanation.surface: A difficulty caused by someone who likes to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tricky puzzle to solve and a person who behaves affectedly to impress others.

clue.text: Forbidden expert, disguised, grabbing snack

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: something disguised has been hid, an old past participle of hide
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: A specialist in disguise snatches a quick bite where it is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prohibited means banned by law or rule, the same as forbidden.

clue.text: Barrage of colossal volume

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the solution comes from within the next words

parts.note: found inside these words

explanation.surface: An enormously loud bombardment.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, and figuratively a burst of attack, like a barrage.

clue.text: Ingredient of salad presented by artist on plate

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a dish is a plate; on puts this piece after the artist in a down clue

explanation.surface: A chef-artist serves a salad on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp, peppery red root vegetable commonly sliced raw into salads.

clue.text: Crime writer's novel has tragic hate consuming one

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so another piece is swallowed into these words
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A detective novel's plot turns on bitter hatred consuming one character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the writer's book, but it is the anagram signal; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was the English author of whodunits featuring Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple.

clue.text: Set out east and cross level area

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a cross is the shape of the letter X
a plain is a flat stretch of land

explanation.surface: A traveller heads off eastwards and crosses a flat stretch of country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as starting a journey, but it is the definition, meaning to lay out clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out a case or argument is to state it clearly and in detail, which is what explaining does.

clue.text: Spoke angrily, having become influenced

parts.note: to grow means to become, as in grow tired
someone influenced has been led

explanation.surface: A person speaks crossly after being swayed by someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To growl is to speak in a low, gruff and hostile tone, like a snarling dog.

clue.text: Conclusion of prayer almost correct

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to correct a text is to amend it

explanation.surface: The ending of a prayer is nearly right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the close of a prayer or hymn, meaning 'so be it'.

clue.text: Unwarranted disorder of August riot

indicators.note: disorder means a jumbled state, so the following letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A summer riot is condemned as needless public disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuitous behaviour is uncalled for, done without any good reason or justification.

clue.text: Pretty busy after a dry run

indicators.note: after means coming later, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: taken as written
TT is teetotal, a dry person who drinks no alcohol
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a busy person is active

explanation.surface: Things get quite hectic after a practice rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty busy' reads as 'quite busy', but 'Pretty' is the definition and 'dry run' splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and attractive are adjectives describing a pleasing, good-looking appearance.

clue.text: Brilliant and smart, securing century, batting until middle of day

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
in cricket a batting side is in
till means until

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter alone

parts.note: the central letter of day

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a sparkling innings, a hundred made while batting until midday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'. 'Brilliant and smart' looks like a pair of synonyms, but 'smart' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Scintillating means sparkling, so it describes dazzlingly clever or lively talk or performance.

clue.text: Airmen get trained and develop

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Air force recruits are drilled and grow into their roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed germinates when it starts to sprout and grow, so the verb means begin to develop.

clue.text: Base that is held by criminal not yielding

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so these pieces go within the other
criminal means crooked, so the letters of the following word are bent out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a bed is a base, as in a bed of rock
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A defiant criminal who won't give in holds a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not yielding' reads as the definition of a stubborn criminal, but 'not' is fodder and 'yielding' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person yields to commands, compliant and submissive rather than resistant.

clue.text: Book following mad hero's search involving old sea creature

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end
to involve is to take in, so one word encloses another
mad means crazy and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A book about a crazed hero's quest for some ancient monster of the deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in hero's is ignored, as crossword punctuation usually is; the old letter goes in before the scramble, and the book letter stays outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The horseshoe crab is a marine arthropod with a hard, hoof-shaped shell, a living fossil.

clue.text: Carve stone inlaid with copper disc

indicators.note: inlaid means set into a surface, so the later pieces are set inside the first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
an LP is a long-playing record, a disc

explanation.surface: A craftsman carves a stone decorated with a copper disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to shape a figure by carving stone or wood, the sculptor's craft.

clue.text: Cartoon clowns stumble

parts.note: comics are comedians, people who clown about
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: Circus clowns take a pratfall, like figures in a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a sequence of drawn cartoon panels telling a short story in a newspaper.

clue.text: Drive miles round hill

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
O is round in shape
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A motorist travels miles around a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal, but it simply supplies the circle-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, an old-fashioned verb for driving.

clue.text: Gain diamonds in turn

parts.note: to gain a prize is to win it
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player picks up diamonds when it is their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the wordplay but simply joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a clock or a handle is to turn it round and round, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fables not without odd features too

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered characters leaves only the even-placed ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Fables, too, are not lacking in strange characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are adverbs meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Note start of tour through north of Baltic state

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of tour
via means by way of, through
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A musical tour passes through the north of a Baltic country.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvian is the adjective for Latvia, the Baltic republic between Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: Secure, holding nerve about cultivation

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to secure with a knot is to tie

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: gall is nerve or cheek

explanation.surface: Someone gathers their nerve to fasten something to do with farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparing of land for crops by ploughing and harrowing, a synonym for cultivation.

clue.text: Abrupt arbiter settled cases

indicators.note: cases is a verb here: the words settle around and enclose the solution within them

parts.note: found inside these words

explanation.surface: A curt referee settles disputes quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like the legal disputes the arbiter settled, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief to the point of curtness, so it is abrupt in manner.

clue.text: Evocative colour Oscar supplied

parts.note: red is a colour
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something lent has been supplied for a time

explanation.surface: A film award ceremony provides a colourful, memorable atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means strongly suggestive or reminiscent of something, bringing it to mind.
